title: A New Editor for London’s International Desk
body_markdown:
Aurelien Breeden, a stalwart of our Paris bureau as a reporter, is now an editor on the International desk. Read more from editors Philip Pan, Adrienne Carter and Matt Surman.


Aurelien Breeden, a stalwart of our Paris bureau as a reporter for more than a decade, is turning his talents to editing and joining the International desk in London.


He has already impressed us with his smart and in-depth work on an array of stories, editing spot news on Ukraine, handling big visuals pieces and enthusiastically jumping into the news fray of the live blog. He has even been lured back into reporting when duty calls, including for a gripping account of


[a deadly fire in Switzerland](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/04/world/europe/crans-montana-victims.html) .


Aurelien joined the Paris bureau in 2014, writing stories big and small about French politics, culture, society, foreign policy and more. He reported on two presidential races and three parliamentary elections, on the


[fire that tore through Notre-Dame Cathedral](https://www.nytimes.com/2019/04/15/world/europe/notre-dame-fire.html) and


[the monument’s yearslong reconstruction](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/12/06/world/europe/notre-dame-paris-france.html) , on widespread protests against pension overhauls and on some of the


[deadliest](https://www.nytimes.com/2015/11/15/world/europe/paris-terrorist-attacks.html) terrorist attacks in France’s history and


[their lasting legacy](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/13/world/europe/france-paris-terrorist-attacks-anniversary.html) .


“For many years Aurelien was the reference for the Paris bureau: the calm, quick, authoritative, all-knowledgeable, uncannily sourced, diligently accurate colleague to whom everyone turned,” said Roger Cohen, the former Paris bureau chief. “He has a temperament rare in journalism. Ever considerate, unrufflable in crisis, generous, Aurelien is a journalist who combines wit and wisdom as, ever so gently, he raises the game of all around him.”


Aurelien is a dual French-American citizen and grew up a Foreign Service brat – born in Paris, but not raised there. He lived in countries including the United Kingdom, the United States, Tunisia and France, then settled in the French capital. He graduated from Sciences Po with a dual master’s degree in journalism and international affairs and later interned at the Paris bureau. He will be based in London.


— Phil, Adrienne and Matt
